hook.line: In Bogotá the apology often comes first and the explanation second. The trick is to say what you are sorry for in one short phrase. Tomás has to apologise to a café full of customers for the noise of the builders.
hook.en: Sorry for the inconvenience. (to a group)

examples.es: Disculpa que no te haya saludado antes.
examples.en: Sorry I didn't say hello earlier. (to a friend)
Sorry for the inconvenience. (to a group)

examples.es: Disculpe que lo moleste a esta hora.
examples.en: Sorry to bother you at this hour. (formal)
Sorry for the delay. (to a friend)

examples.es: Perdona que no te haya llamado.
examples.en: Sorry I haven't called you. (to a friend)

examples.es: Disculpen que no les haya avisado.
examples.en: Sorry I didn't let you all know.

rule:
After *Disculpa* (or *Perdona*) say what you are sorry for:

+ a noun for something that happened: *Disculpa la demora.*, *Disculpen las molestias.*
+ *que no te haya* + the *-ado* word, for something you did or didn't do: *Disculpa que no te haya saludado.*
+ *que* + a "wish" verb, for what you are doing right now: *Disculpe que lo moleste.*

Use *Disculpa* with a friend, *Disculpe* with *usted*, *Disculpen* with a group. English just says "sorry I…". In Spanish the *que* needs the special verb: *haya saludado*, *moleste*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *haya saludado* the present perfect subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *Disculpa* or *Disculpe*. Sorry for the delay (to a friend). ___ la demora. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: With a friend you use *tú*, so the verb is *Disculpa*.

yourTurn.prompt: Sorry for the inconvenience. (to a group)
Choose *haya saludado* or *saludé*. Sorry I didn't say hello earlier (to a friend). Disculpa que no te ___ antes. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Disculpa que no te haya saludado antes.
accept: Perdona que no te haya saludado antes.
yourTurn.why: After *disculpa que* the verb takes the special form: *haya saludado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Sorry to bother you at this hour. (formal)
yourTurn.answer: Disculpe que lo moleste a esta hora.
accept: Perdone que lo moleste a esta hora.
yourTurn.why: *Usted* takes *Disculpe*, and *moleste* is the wish form.

yourTurn.prompt: Sorry I haven't called you. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Perdona que no te haya llamado.
accept: Disculpa que no te haya llamado.
yourTurn.why: *Que no te haya llamado* says what you didn't do.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal: Disculpa que te interrumpa. Say it to someone you call *usted*.
yourTurn.why: *Usted* changes both the first verb (*Disculpe*) and the pronoun (*lo*).

yourTurn.prompt: Sorry I didn't let you all know.
yourTurn.answer: Disculpen que no les haya avisado.
accept: Perdonen que no les haya avisado.

pitfalls.wrong: Disculpa que no te saludé antes.
pitfalls.right: Disculpa que no te haya saludado antes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *disculpa que* Spanish wants *haya saludado*, not the plain past.

pitfalls.wrong: Disculpe que te moleste a esta hora.
pitfalls.right: Disculpe que lo moleste a esta hora.
pitfalls.why: Keep the same register: *Disculpe* goes with *lo*, not *te*.
A noun for something that happened needs no *que*: *Disculpa la demora*.

personal: Think of a small thing you got wrong this week. Apologise for it: *Disculpa que no…* or *Disculpa la…*
